text.p: These are the leading stories in the Malawi press on Monday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Malawi President Bakili Muluzi called off a meeting with the opposition Alliance for Democracy (AFORD), scheduled for Monday, after his invitation for talks was leaked to a local newspaper.
- Education Minister Donton Mkandawire said he has taken tough measures to curb corruption at schools and ensure secondary school entrants do so on merit.

- The main opposition Malawi Congress Party (MCP) has questioned the Supreme Court's actions to uphold a bill passed by parliament which will allow for the take over of former president Kamuzu Banda's Press Trust.
- Four armed men on Friday hijacked a one-tonne truck before going on a crime spree.

- Former police officer Augustine Likaomba, acquitted in 1995 together with former president Kamuzu Banda on charges of plotting to murder four senior politicians, is struggling to receive benefits after being retired from service in 1994.
- The Malawi Against Polio organisation plans to lease crutches to encourage people to return them after use.
